_readme: Single source of truth for what CI builds. scripts/versions-matrix.sh turns this
into the GitHub Actions matrices; scripts/check-versions.sh enforces the
invariants that used to be someone's job to remember. Bumping a version is an
edit here plus the matching ARG default in that image's Dockerfile - and the
checker fails the build if you do only one.
Per image: 'platforms' maps a build platform to the runner pool that builds it
natively (a platform with no pool would leave runs-on empty and the leg would
never start). 'builds' lists the variants published for that image; 'tag' is the
version tag in GHCR, 'args' are passed as --build-arg, and exactly one variant
carries 'primary': true - that one also gets 'latest' and 'sha-<commit>'.
An image built on another one names it in 'base' and points each variant at a
'base_tag' that must exist among the base image's tags. CI passes the base as a
digest through 'base_arg', so the tag here is what binds a variant to the exact
base version its own tag advertises.
'pin' is passed as a build arg like 'args', but is checked differently: its
values are commit SHAs, so they cannot appear in the tag. ESP-Matter publishes
no git tags - only moving release/* branches - so a branch names a line, not a
release: release/v1.5 carried specification v1.5 at one commit and v1.5.1 at
another. The pin is what makes the image tag mean something and a rebuild
reproduce the same tree. 'upstream_branch' records where the pin came from;
./scripts/update-matter-ref.sh advances it.
The idf-v5.4.1 line (and the Matter v1.4.2 variant on it) is kept building on
purpose while projects still depend on those tags - it is not the primary and
gets no `latest`. Drop both entries once nothing pins them; the published tags
survive in GHCR either way, they just stop being rebuilt.
Not listed here: ARGs that CI never passes (ESP32_PLATFORM_VERSION,
NATIVE_PLATFORM_VERSION, UNITY_VERSION in images/platformio/Dockerfile). Their
Dockerfile default is the only source of truth and is bumped there. The package
pins inside a Dockerfile - the esp-idf test harness and esptool - are the same
regime, and they could not live here even if that were desirable: every value in
'args' has to appear in the variant's tag, and a harness version never does.
./scripts/check-pins.sh is what checks them instead.
